[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Secrets Management — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHOULD have an architectural capability to generate short-lived, workload-specific credentials on demand and inject them into application processes at runtime, reducing the risk window associated with long-lived static secrets.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to generate time-limited credentials scoped to the requesting workload identity
- Secure injection of generated credentials into application processes without developer intervention
- Automatic credential expiry and revocation tied to workload lifecycle

**Out of Scope**:
- Storage of static long-lived secrets (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21, which this ABB depends on)
- Certificate issuance for TLS (see Infrastructure Security domain)
- Human user credential management (see Identity Security domain)
- Security controls, configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- Dynamic secrets SHOULD be used in preference to static long-lived credentials wherever the target system supports dynamic credential issuance.
- Dynamically generated credentials SHALL be scoped to the minimum permissions required for the requesting workload's function.
- Credential lifetime SHALL be as short as operationally feasible for the use case.
- Dynamic credential generation SHALL be audited through the Secrets Vault (GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21) audit capability.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#on-demand-credential-generation]

#### On-Demand Credential Generation

**Architectural intent**: Produce unique, short-lived credentials for each workload instance that requests them, eliminating shared static credentials.

**Design guidance**:
- Credential generation SHALL be triggered by an authenticated workload identity request.
- Generated credentials SHALL be unique per workload instance — the same credential SHALL NOT be shared between concurrently running instances.
- Each credential SHALL carry a defined expiry time after which it is automatically invalidated.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#secure-injection]

#### Secure Injection

**Architectural intent**: Deliver generated credentials to the requesting workload without exposing them in the environment in plaintext for longer than necessary.

**Design guidance**:
- Credentials SHOULD be injected at container startup via a sidecar or init-container pattern, not stored in environment configuration files.
- Injected credentials SHOULD be stored in memory only and SHALL NOT be written to the container file system.
- Credential renewal SHOULD be handled automatically before expiry to avoid application interruption.

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credential Request | Inbound | Application Workload | Authenticated request for a dynamic credential |
| Vault Backend | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21 | Credential generation request delegated to vault backend |
| Injected Credential | Outbound | Application Process | Short-lived credential delivered to workload at runtime |
| Target System | Outbound | Database / API / Service | Generated credential used to authenticate to target resource |

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

Dynamic Secrets Injection directly advances the Identity pillar of Zero Trust by ensuring that credentials used for application-to-service authentication are short-lived, workload-scoped, and automatically expiring — removing the long-lived shared secret as a persistent risk.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the IA (Identification and Authentication) family — specifically authenticator management and the reduction of authenticator exposure — and the AC (Access Control) family's intent for least-privilege access through scoped, time-limited credentials.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DSECR-2.7.22.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- Dynamic credential generation requires target systems (databases, APIs, services) to support the credential issuance model; not all systems support this pattern.
- This ABB depends on GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21 for the credential generation backend.
- Credential renewal logic must handle vault unavailability gracefully; architecture must address the failure mode where renewal is not possible before expiry.
